title: A Theory on Flow Matching with Neural Networks
claim: Across many hyperparameter settings, error metrics grow systematically with problem dimension and shrink with learning rate, consistent with the theoretical predictions.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots sharing x-axis, legends at right, shaded seed bands
description: Two side-by-side line plots, each plotting a metric against ambient dimension d from 5 to 50. Panel (a) shows terminal training loss on a log y-axis (about 10 to several thousand). Panel (b) shows sliced Wasserstein-1 distance on a linear y-axis (0 to 15). Each panel has 15 curves, one per width and learning-rate pair. Color encodes learning rate (dark purple for 1e-4, teal for 1e-3, light green for 1e-2). Marker and linestyle encode width (16, 32, 64, 128, 256). Shaded bands show ±1 standard deviation over seeds. Curves rise with d, and the purple curves sit highest. A legend listing all 15 configurations sits to the right of each panel. Captions (a) and (b) with math notation sit below. The eye goes first to the stacked purple, teal and green curve bundles.
caption: Global view of the $5\cdot3\cdot10=150$ cell sweep at $n_{\rm train}=500$, $n_{\rm test}=5000$. Each curve is one $(m,\eta)$ pair; color encodes $\eta$ ($10^{-4}$ darkest, $10^{-2}$ lightest) and marker/linestyle encodes width $m$. Values at the final iterate $t=T=500$; solid lines show the mean and shaded bands show $\pm1$ standard deviation over $10$ independent random seeds. (a) Terminal training loss grows with $d$ and decreases with $\eta$ (Theorem [ref]). (b) Sliced $\overline{W_1}$ grows with $d$ (Theorem [ref]).
abstract: In this work, we develop theoretical foundation for flow matching with neural-network-parameterized conditional velocity fields. We establish convergence guarantees for gradient descent in the over-parameterized 2-layered ReLU neural network regime. We derive generalization bounds for the conditional velocity-field matching objective. Building on these results, we provide Wasserstein-distance guarantees for the samples generated by the induced flow. Our analysis is based on generalization bound for multi-task representation learning with unbounded losses, which may be of independent interest beyond flow-based generative modeling. These theoretical results are validated through extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world image benchmarks. Our code is available at https://github.com/qishuoyin/FlowMatchNN.
